Fuel cells overview

Devices that continuously consume fuel to produce electricity and heat. Explore technology types, fuel cleanliness and electricity sales mechanisms.

Operating principlesHow types are classifiedHydrogen & clean hydrogenHPS·CHPSBusiness evaluation

Are fuel cells storage devices or generators?

Fuel cells directly convert the chemical energy of a fuel and oxidant into electricity through electrochemical reactions. They generate while fuel and air are supplied, unlike secondary batteries that recharge their internal reactants.

Fuel supplyHydrogen or a convertible fuel
Electrochemical reactionElectrons and ions follow different paths
Electricity & heatProducts depend on the fuel

The basic reaction using hydrogen directly is 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O + electricity + heat. Systems that reform natural gas into hydrogen, or use carbon-containing fuels, can also emit CO₂.

Names such as PEMFC and SOFC refer to the electrolyte

Fuel cells are classified mainly by electrolyte type, which determines the mobile ion, operating temperature and fuel options. DMFC emphasizes the direct use of methanol, rather than a particular electrolyte class.

TypeElectrolyte / ionFeatures & typical applications
Polymer electrolyte membrane fuel cell · PEMFCPolymer membrane · H⁺Relatively low operating temperature and responsive output. Vehicles, mobile and distributed power.
Solid oxide fuel cell · SOFCSolid oxide · usually O²⁻High-temperature operation with fuel flexibility and useful heat. Stationary generation.
Phosphoric acid fuel cell · PAFCPhosphoric acid · H⁺Stationary combined heat and power. Heat recovery and system operation are important.
Molten carbonate fuel cell · MCFCMolten carbonate · CO₃²⁻High-temperature operation for large stationary generation and heat use.
Alkaline fuel cell · AFCAlkaline solution · OH⁻A traditional class sensitive to CO₂ contamination, used in space and other applications.
Direct methanol fuel cell · DMFCUsually a polymer membrane · H⁺ / direct methanol supplyConvenient liquid fuel. Portable and remote power; the reaction produces CO₂.

Are hydrogen and clean-hydrogen fuel cells separate technology classes?

A hydrogen fuel cell uses hydrogen as fuel. Clean hydrogen is a certification concept based on greenhouse-gas emissions from hydrogen production and related stages. A clean-hydrogen fuel cell is not a separate electrolyte class; it is a fuel cell using certified clean hydrogen.

Separate device emissions from fuel emissions. A direct-hydrogen fuel cell produces water, but fossil-based hydrogen production means lifecycle greenhouse-gas emissions are not necessarily zero. Certification and its accounting boundary matter more than hydrogen color labels.

Korea's clean-hydrogen threshold is greenhouse-gas emissions per kilogram of hydrogen of no more than 4 kg CO₂e. CO₂e converts different greenhouse gases to a common carbon-dioxide equivalent. Check the applicable notice and certification criteria for boundaries, grades and transport-related provisions.

National Law Information Center · Clean-hydrogen certification noticeIndustry ministry · Korean certification criteria

What are HPS and CHPS?

HPS (Hydrogen Portfolio Standard) and CHPS (Clean Hydrogen Portfolio Standard) are terms used to describe hydrogen and clean-hydrogen generation obligations. When searching for the actual markets, use the official names General Hydrogen Power Generation Tender Market and Clean Hydrogen Power Generation Tender Market. HPS sometimes refers to the wider hydrogen-generation framework, so distinguish the context.

These markets competitively purchase electricity produced from hydrogen or hydrogen compounds. They are distinct from hydrogen purchasing or fuel-cell equipment procurement. Korea Power Exchange operates the tenders, and generators submit prices and project plans for evaluation.

CategoryGeneral hydrogen-generation tender marketClean-hydrogen-generation tender market
PurposePromote distributed hydrogen generation and competitionExpand clean-hydrogen use and reduce greenhouse gases
FuelGeneral hydrogen generation without mandatory clean-hydrogen certification; consult the notice for eligible fuelsFuel meeting Korea's clean-hydrogen certification criteria
EvaluationBid price plus grid impacts and industrial/economic contributionsBid price plus clean-hydrogen grade, fuel-supply reliability and industrial/economic contributions
Examples announced for the 2025 opening1,300 GWh annually / 20-year term3,000 GWh annually / 15-year term
Relationship to fuel cellsAn electricity sales route to assess for fuel-cell projectsSeparately assess fuel certification and other tender requirements
CHPS is not exclusively a fuel-cell market. It covers generation using clean hydrogen or hydrogen compounds, so other generation technologies may qualify under the tender requirements. Fuel-cell technology or hydrogen use alone does not guarantee eligibility or an award.

Distinguish the proposed 2026 changes. In its June 8, 2026 advance notice, the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment proposed annual volumes of 500 GWh for clean hydrogen and 930 GWh for general hydrogen, exclusion of coal–ammonia co-firing support, and stronger environmental evaluation for general hydrogen. This describes the proposal at that date; subsequent final notices and tenders govern actual participation.

Which costs matter for generation projects?

Assess equipment cost (KRW/kW), fuel, efficiency, utilization, stack replacement and maintenance, heat sales and electricity sales terms together. Storage-capacity cost (KRW/kWh) and generating-capacity cost (KRW/kW) are different metrics.

For each project, combine tender revenue with fuel, maintenance and financing costs to calculate generation cost and cash flow. These are business evaluation criteria, not a claim that fuel cells are always cheaper than thermal generation.
